comment: Ground truth for the taint precision probe suite (analysis-strategy.md §5.5). One family per precision axis. Lines are 1-BASED source lines of `print(...)` call statements (the lifter's loc.line is 0-based; the runner adds 1). expect: tp = real flow, must hit; clean = no flow, must NOT hit (FP guard); fp = no flow but the CURRENT rung hits (EXPECTED false positive; closes_at_rung says which ladder rung should kill it, null = structural/wontfix); fn = real flow the current rung misses (KNOWN false negative; closes_at_rung says which rung should catch it). The runner FAILS on any deviation in either direction — an expected-fp/fn that stops reproducing means the ladder moved and this file must be updated deliberately. HISTORY: annotated at rung 0 (t-P1; tp=11 fp=4 fn=4). Rung 1 (t-P2, the on-demand alias engine + points_to-fed call-graph refinement + heap-fact summary endpoints, default rung now 1) flipped: a4 fp→clean (store base refined to mkobj's alloc site, disjoint from o's), a5 fp→clean (balanced call/return hop proves p===o, strong update kills the taint), b3 fn→tp (param-callee bridged to the caller's AllocClosure body), e5 fn→tp (Object.assign alias-flow endpoint matches heap facts by positive points-to intersection). b2 evaluated honestly and RE-TAGGED rung 1→2 (environment identity, not heap aliasing — see its rationale). New table: tp=13 fp=2 fn=2. t-P3 (prototype-chain summary lookup): e6–e10 added — receiver-typed builtin calls (local alloc array, own-method shadow FP control, global-store provenance string, for-of iterator protocol, repeat-count clean guard). New table: tp=16 fp=3 fn=2. t-P4 (full gap propagator): e11–e16 added — the Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter gap trio (gap enter/return channels, param-callee resolution through the may-direction arm, the unresolved-callback honest fallback); e13 is an EXPECTED fp (unknown-base may-alias on the VM-allocated map result, closes at rung 2; the gap return channel itself is pinned silent by the mechanism twin). New table: tp=20 fp=4 fn=2. t-P5 (miss-log-driven second tier): e17–e23 added — String.prototype.replace's dual form (string replacement Base+Param(1)→Return, pattern is control; function replacement via the t-P4 gap machinery with the EMPTY-chain return channel), RegExp.prototype.test (no-flow verdict, constructor-result family arm), String.prototype.split / Array.prototype.join (content-derived; separator asymmetry), parseInt/Number.parseInt (content-derived, non-exclusive per the exclusive-policy review), Object.assign's result identity. New table: tp=30 fp=4 fn=2. Rung 2 (t-P6, the whole-module context-sensitive PTA — 1-call-site contexts, per-object field sensitivity, delta worklist, on-the-fly call-graph co-evolution; default rung now 2) flipped: b2 fp→clean (the lexical-environment identity channel: NewLexEnv-site-keyed env objects + closure capture linkage separate the colliding (0,0) slots), c4 fn→tp (the stored closure's element points-to resolves the call edge through the co-evolution), d4 fn→tp (global-object points-to resolves the top-level thrower's edge), e7 fp→clean (the own-method store resolves the callee to the USER body — body-step precedence over the prototype-path summary; the pop summary no longer applies and its counter expectation was removed), e13 fp→clean (t-P4's registered idea LANDED: a summary result no static flow reaches is a fresh container keyed by its call site, killing the unknown-base wildcard). c2 stays fp — wontfix-structural (see its rationale). New table: tp=32 fp=1 fn=0.

es2abc.why: Newest pinned image version (precision axes are version-independent; the suite is not a version matrix). Baseline profile = --opt-level=0, the least-transformed bytecode, and it still carries the line-number table (verified: lifted Inst.loc present, 0-based). Script mode matches the corpus' local-fixture compiles.

config_notes: builtin_summaries on, seed_all_functions on, native_identity on — all defaults. Every probe declares `var TAINT = "tainted"` at top level (script mode → global record) so the VM run is clean AND every read compiles to TryGetGlobal("TAINT"), which is the source.

probes.rationale: Same alloc site, store then load of one field — the rung-0 baseline heap case (site-keyed facts meet at the key).
Distinct alloc sites, same field name — rung-0 site keying must keep them apart (disjoint non-empty site sets ⇒ no alias).
Store through a Mov alias — the def-chain walk resolves p to o's site, so the store/load keys meet.

Store through a call-result (unknown) base keyed the fact with an EMPTY site set at rung 0, may-aliasing every load of the field (the FP this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED clean at rung 1 (t-P2): the engine's memoized backward points_to hops the call into mkobj and keys the store with mkobj's alloc site — disjoint from o's site, so the hit dies.

Sanitizing store through an unproven alias (call result) was a WEAK update at rung 0 — the taint survived even though p === o at runtime (the FP this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED clean at rung 1 (t-P2): the balanced call/return hop resolves p's points_to to o's single alloc site (id returns its formal; the context stack binds it to THIS call's argument), so the update is strong and kills the taint.

Phi of the aliased object and a fresh one — the site union still intersects o's site (weak update path exercised). Runtime never takes the fresh-object branch (TAINT.length is 7), so the flow is real.
Captured variable promoted to a lexical-env slot by es2abc; the LexVar fact is a state base and crosses the resolved direct call edge into the closure body.

LexVar keys were function-agnostic (level, slot) pairs — innocent's slot-(0,0) capture merged with main's tainted slot-(0,0) capture across resolved call edges (the FP rungs 0–1 recorded). FLIPPED clean at rung 2 (t-P6): the PTA's lexical-environment channel treats NewLexEnv instructions as environment allocation sites and reconstructs each closure's captured chain (the env stack at its AllocClosure/DefineFunc site, to a fixed point). PutLexVar/GetLexVar facts key by env-site Heap(env).[AnyIndex] when the env answer is precise, so main's env (InstId 0) and innocent's env (InstId 28) no longer meet; imprecise accesses fall back to the legacy (level, slot) key on write and to a may-direction any-env-site match on read (sound).

The callback is invoked through a PARAMETER callee (register's cb) — unresolved at rung 0, so no call edge carried the captured taint into cb's body (the FN this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED tp at rung 1 (t-P2): CallGraph::refine_with_points_to asks the engine for the callee value's sites; the unbalanced caller fan-out traces register's cb param to main's AllocClosure site, the bridge maps it to cb's DefineFunc body, and the solver steps in (§5.4's one engine, two consumers).

Phi of two closures — set-valued resolution steps into BOTH; the real flow through id is found. The konst over-approximation is invisible at sink granularity because the runtime path really goes through id (TAINT.length is 7 > 0). (The N66 frame-slot binding fix — args[i] -> params[3+i] under the vendored 0xF callType default — landed in problem.rs call_flow; this probe was the red-first evidence and flipped to TP when the fix landed.)

A USER-DEFINED top-level `print` takes over the global binding; name-keyed sink matching keys on TryGetGlobal("print"), so the sink fires on a call whose binding is user code. EVALUATED at rung 2 (t-P6): the PTA now RESOLVES the callee to the user body (the global-object bucket has it), so the edge is known — but sink semantics are deliberately name-keyed (the corpus' ~97% unknown-callee reality is why name keying exists), and distinguishing the host builtin from a user redefinition is a SINK-SPEC question (host-binding provenance), not a points-to question. Stays fp, wontfix-structural; registered as a sink-semantics backlog item beyond the alias ladder.

Method-valued callee off a local object: dispatch unresolved at rung 0 (no receiver typing), the identity heuristic carries arg taint to the call result. TP via the fallback ladder, not via dispatch — documents what currently saves unresolved method calls.

Callee loaded from an array element — dispatch unresolved at rungs 0–1, no call edge entered the stored closure (the FN they recorded). FLIPPED tp at rung 2 (t-P6): the array's Dynamic bucket gains the closure object at the StorePropDyn, the LoadPropDyn reads it back (per-object field sensitivity), and the on-the-fly co-evolution wires the call edge into the closure body — §5.5's APAK axis landed.
throw→handler is the ONLY route from source to sink — intraprocedural exception dispatch (T5).
The thrown value is clean; a tainted local stays live across the try but is never thrown nor printed. Two clean sinks (catch binding, normal path) — FP guards.

Taint thrown inside a RESOLVED callee lands on the caller's catch binding — return_flow Throw wiring (T5/T10). (The N66 frame-slot binding fix — args[i] -> params[3+i] under the vendored 0xF callType default — landed in problem.rs call_flow; this probe was the red-first evidence and flipped to TP when the fix landed.)

The thrower is a top-level function — a global binding, so the call edge was unresolved at rungs 0–1 (the corpus' ~97% unknown-callee reality) and the tainted argument never entered boom (the FN they recorded). FLIPPED tp at rung 2 (t-P6): func_main_0's StoreGlobal puts boom's closure object into the global-object bucket, TryGetGlobal reads it back, the co-evolution wires the edge, and the throw rides the return_flow Throw wiring to the catch binding (the d3 mechanism).
Exclusive summary application: JSON.stringify's param(0)→return flow carries the taint. The counter assertion proves the SUMMARY fired (not the identity heuristic).

Exclusive pure-test summary: Object.is's result is a fresh boolean, operand taint killed on the call-to-return edge. Proves summary application beats the native identity heuristic (which would otherwise taint the result).

No summary, resolved callee with a body — the solver steps INTO the body. The counter assertion proves body_step (the flow does not ride the identity heuristic). (The N66 frame-slot binding fix — args[i] -> params[3+i] under the vendored 0xF callType default — landed in problem.rs call_flow; this probe was the red-first evidence and flipped to TP when the fix landed.)

No summary, external-but-named callee — conservative keep + identity heuristic (fallback ladder rung 3). The named-miss assertion proves NO summary fired for parseFloat. Sentinel history: parseInt until t-P5 registered it (the miss log drove its summary); parseFloat is its deliberately-unregistered sibling.

Object.assign's alias_flow matched WHOLE-VALUE taint on param(1) only — the source literal's FIELD taint is heap-keyed and never entered the target (the FN this probe recorded at rung 0). FLIPPED tp (t-P2): summary flow endpoints now match heap facts whose site set positively intersects the endpoint value's site resolution. The match is NOT oracle-gated — it fires whenever site resolution knows the argument's sites (the rung-0 local walk suffices for this locally-allocated literal; the rung-1 engine matters when the argument needs the interprocedural query). A/B evidence: e5 flips at BOTH oracle rungs; a4/a5/b3 flip only at rung 1.

t-P3 prototype-resolution path: a local AllocArray receiver types Array.prototype; push's alias flow tags the [AnyIndex] element channel and pop's Field([AnyIndex])→Return flow carries it to the popped value. TP.

An array with its OWN pop typed Array.prototype at rungs 0–1 (the shadow store was invisible at the method load), so the BUILTIN pop summary fired on a call that runs user code (the recorded FP). FLIPPED clean at rung 2 (t-P6): the PTA resolves the StoreProp into the LoadProp — the callee's points-to is the user's closure — and the classification precedence (a resolved USER BODY beats the prototype-path summary) steps into the body, which returns 7 (clean). The Array.prototype.pop summary no longer applies at this site (its counter expectation removed; push still applies). The c2 lesson stands: what was structural name-collision becomes value-flow resolution.

t-P3 global-store provenance: the receiver is a local alias of the TAINT global; points-to is opaque through global loads, but the module's stores of TAINT (a string literal) type the receiver String.prototype through the flow-insensitive global-record scan; charCodeAt's Base→Return flow carries the content taint. TP.

t-P3 for-of protocol: getiterator over an AllocArray types Iterator.prototype; the array's [AnyIndex] element taint re-keys onto the iterator at the GetIterator flow rule and rides Iterator.prototype.next's Field([AnyIndex])→Return flow into the {value,done} wrapper; the .value read picks it up. TP.

t-P3 repeat-count FP guard: the constant receiver types String.prototype; repeat's summary flows Base→Return only, so the TAINTED COUNT goes nowhere — pins summary application beating the native-identity heuristic (which would taint the result), e2's prototype-path analogue. Ground truth: "x".repeat("tainted") is "" — clean.

t-P4 full gap propagator: forEach's callback resolves to a local closure; the array's [AnyIndex] element taint enters the callback's formal 0 through the gap enter rules and the print inside the body fires. TP.
t-P4 gap return channel: map's callback returns its tainted formal; the gap return wires it onto the result array's [AnyIndex] elements and the indexed read fires. TP.

map's callback ignores its parameter and returns a constant — the result elements carry no REAL taint. The FP rungs 0–1 recorded: the map result is VM-allocated (no keyed site), so the indexed load met the SOURCE array's Heap(site).[AnyIndex] fact through the load rule's unknown-base may-alias wildcard. FLIPPED clean at rung 2 (t-P6) — t-P4's registered idea LANDED: a summary result no static flow reaches (map has no Param/Base/Field→Return* flow; the gap return channel keys its facts precisely) is a FRESH container keyed by its call site, so the wildcard no longer fires. e23's Object.assign keeps its aliasing result (Param(i)→Return inflow ⇒ not fresh) and e12's real flow is untouched (the gap-returned taint is a LOCAL fact on the result value).
t-P4: filter's predicate return taints nothing (return channel None); the result's elements are the base's kept elements via the static Field([AnyIndex])→ReturnField([AnyIndex]) flow. TP.

t-P4 honest fallback: the callback is an opaque global load — no gap edge, the element taint never enters user code (mini-gap tag only; gap_sites_unresolved records the site). forEach's result is undefined. Clean.

t-P4 points-to arm: the callback reaches the gap site through a resolved local helper's parameter — the rung-1 engine's caller fan-out resolves it to the caller's closure alloc, and the receiver param types Array through the same engine. TP.

String.prototype.replace, string-replacement form (t-P5; the corpus' top actionable miss, regexp.js ×18). The result derives from the base (non-matched parts) and the replacement (inserted verbatim); the pattern SELECTS — control, not content (the e10 repeat-count discipline). Line 15 pins the summary against the identity heuristic, which would taint the result through the tainted pattern operand.

String.prototype.replace, function-replacement form — the t-P4 gap mechanism on a dual-form summary. Gap enter: the callback's match formal derives from the base (line 13's print fires inside the callback). Gap return: the callback's RETURN is inserted into the result string — the EMPTY-chain return channel (the result is a string, not map's [AnyIndex] array). Line 16: a tainted pattern over a clean base taints nothing (control, not content; the callback runs on a clean match).

RegExp.prototype.test (the corpus' r.test ×18) — a pure match VERDICT: the fresh boolean carries no content (the Object.is discipline). The tainted haystack must NOT taint the verdict; the clean sink pins the no-flow summary against the identity heuristic. The regexp literal compiles to `new RegExp(...)`, so the receiver types through the t-P5 constructor-result family arm.

String.prototype.split (canonical preemptive, corpus-freq 0): the pieces derive from the base's content (Base→Return; the element read cuts one step). The separator is REMOVED — control, not content: line 12 pins the summary against the identity heuristic.

Array.prototype.join (canonical preemptive; the corpus' only join use is a runtime-not-applicable fixture): the joined string carries the element taint (Field([AnyIndex])→Return, the push-tagged channel) AND the separator, which is inserted VERBATIM (Param(0)→Return) — the asymmetry with split's removed separator is the semantics. Line 14 is the clean control.

parseInt / Number.parseInt (canonical preemptive, corpus-freq 0): content-derived digit parse — the number derives from the string's content (the charCodeAt discipline); the radix is control (line 12 pins against the identity heuristic). NON-exclusive per the t-P5 exclusive-policy review (a pure READ of its operand: killSource would FN SSA re-use; the callee-body kill is vacuous for a native).

Object.assign's result identity (t-P5 deepening): the result IS param 0, so Param(i)→Return carries the source literal's tainted field through the fresh-object result — the `let o = Object.assign({}, src)` shape. Single-assign only: a second assign's unknown-base result would meet the first's heap fact through the load rule's may-alias wildcard (the e13 lesson), so the clean control lives in the mechanism twin (assign_result_carries_source_taint).
